title: Rename offset fields from *Byte to *Char for semantic honesty
context: JavaScript string indexing (.length, .indexOf(), .index) counts UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes. The fields startByte/endByte/atByte in helm.ts and k8sManifest.ts were misleadingly named, implying byte precision they never had.
decision: Rename all offset fields to *Char in helm.ts and k8sManifest.ts to accurately reflect they contain character indices. Map these *Char values into the shared ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall arrays' *Byte fields in indexer.ts, with explicit comments documenting the semantic mismatch (those shared arrays' *Byte fields are also character offsets in practice, tracked separately as issue #84).
consequences: Field naming now honestly reflects actual semantics — prevents future confusion about precision
Callers must understand the *Char → *Byte mapping in indexer.ts; documented via comments
Values unchanged; purely a semantic clarification with no behavior change
Reveals a pre-existing issue: merged arrays still have misleading *Byte names (tracked separately)
alternatives_rejected: Keep *Byte naming despite inaccuracy — masks the real problem and allows future bugs
Convert to actual UTF-8 byte offsets — unnecessary complexity and performance cost
Leave unaddressed — continued silent semantic mismatch between field names and values
